tracks.title: Get in
tracks.sub: the R1, the iPhone, the iPad

lessons.title: On the R1, no other device
lessons.text:
Open Termux from the R1's app list. It opens straight into your Linux at the r1@localhost prompt.
The key row above the keyboard: Esc, Ctrl, Tab, Up, Down. Up and Down bring back your last commands. Slash and dash are under ?123.
Pinch the text to resize it. Type exit to leave Linux and land in plain Termux.

lessons.title: From the iPhone or iPad: a terminal
lessons.text:
In Easy SSH: host = the R1's address (home Wi-Fi, or the Router address when on the PL R1 hotspot), port 2222, user r1, your password from your notes.
Restoration: tmux, so a dropped connection comes back to where you were.
Ctrl is the ^ key in Easy SSH's row: tap ^ then c to stop a program.

lessons.title: From the iPad: the full desktop
lessons.text:
In RealVNC: R1 Linux appears by name, or type the R1's address with :5901. Your desktop password is in your notes.
Scaling: Fit to screen. Leave 'resize remote screen' off.
Pictures you make are in Home > Pictures > pieces.

lessons.title: Away from home
lessons.text:
On the R1, swipe down and tap Hotspot (the first tile). Join PL R1 on the iPad or iPhone.
Use the Router address from the iPad's Wi-Fi details in Easy SSH or RealVNC.
The hotspot turns itself off after 10 minutes with nobody on it. Installing new things needs internet (home Wi-Fi or your phone's hotspot).

lessons.title: Night 1: where am I
lessons.text:
pwd: the folder you are in
ls -la: what is in it, hidden files too
cd / ; ls: the top of the whole system
cd ~: back home
man ls: the manual, offline

lessons.title: Night 2: files
lessons.text: nano notes.txt: write a line, Ctrl+O Enter to save, Ctrl+X to leave
run: cp notes.txt copy.txt ; mv copy.txt renamed.txt ; rm renamed.txt

lessons.title: Night 3: who and what
lessons.text:
whoami ; id: you, and your groups
ls -l notes.txt: the rwx letters are permissions
htop: live view of what is running (q to quit)
df -h ; free -h: disk and memory

lessons.title: Night 4: installing (needs internet)
lessons.text: Type each line, press Enter, read what comes back.

lessons.title: Night 5: scripts
lessons.text: nano hello.sh: write:  #!/bin/bash

lessons.title: Night 6: git
lessons.text: Type each line, press Enter, read what comes back.
run: git config --global user.name "you" ; git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
echo "day one" > log.txt ; git add log.txt ; git commit -m "first"

lessons.title: Night 7: a tiny server
lessons.text: On your iPhone (same Wi-Fi or the PL R1 hotspot), open Safari:: http://<R1 address>:8000
run: On your iPhone (same Wi-Fi or the PL R1 hotspot), open Safari:
Ctrl+C to stop. That is what a cloud server does, in your pocket.

tracks.title: Code
tracks.sub: twelve lessons, print to generative art

lessons.title: 1. Your first program
lessons.text:
A program is a list of instructions the computer follows top to bottom.
DO
  learn run          runs this lesson's code
  learn edit         opens it in nano. Change the words, Ctrl+O Enter to save, Ctrl+X to leave
  learn run          again: your change is on screen
TRY
  Change the line of ~ to a line of = . Make it longer.
NEXT: learn next
lessons.code:
# Lesson 1: print puts text on the screen.
GOLD, RESET = "\033[38;2;201;168;76m", "\033[0m"
print(GOLD + "~" * 30)
print("Watch this.")
print("~" * 30 + RESET)

lessons.title: 2. Loops: doing a thing many times
lessons.text:
A loop repeats. range(10) counts 0 to 9.
DO
  learn run , then learn edit
TRY
  Change 10 to 20. Change "*" to "o". Make the triangle point the other way (hint: 10 - i).
NEXT: learn next
lessons.code:
# Lesson 2: a for loop draws a triangle, one row per turn.
GOLD, RESET = "\033[38;2;201;168;76m", "\033[0m"
for i in range(10):
    print(GOLD + "*" * (i + 1) + RESET)

lessons.title: 3. A curve made of text
lessons.text:
math.sin goes smoothly up and down between -1 and 1: the shape behind every curve you draw.
Here each row's position comes from sin, so the stars trace a wave.
TRY
  Change 15 (how wide it swings) and 3 (how stretched it is). Change range(40) to range(80).
NEXT: learn next
lessons.code:
# Lesson 3: math.sin turns a row number into a sideways position.
import math
GOLD, RESET = "\033[38;2;201;168;76m", "\033[0m"
for y in range(40):
    x = int(20 + 15 * math.sin(y / 3))
    print(GOLD + " " * x + "*" + RESET)

lessons.title: 4. Make it move
lessons.text:
Animation is the same picture drawn again, a little different, many times a second.
time.sleep waits between frames. \033[H moves the cursor home so each frame draws over the last.
Ctrl+C stops it (on Easy SSH: tap ^ then c).
TRY
  Change 0.05 (speed). Change the * to a word.
NEXT: learn next
lessons.code:
# Lesson 4: a wave that moves. Ctrl+C to stop.
import math, time
GOLD, RESET = "\033[38;2;201;168;76m", "\033[0m"
t = 0
try:
    while True:
        lines = []
        for y in range(20):
            x = int(20 + 15 * math.sin(y / 3 + t))
            lines.append(" " * x + "*" + " " * (40 - x))
        print("\033[H" + GOLD + "\n".join(lines) + RESET)
        t += 0.2
        time.sleep(0.05)
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    print(RESET)

lessons.title: 5. Functions: name a thing so you can reuse it
lessons.text:
def makes a function: a named recipe. Call it with different numbers and get different results.
TRY
  Add a third call: wave(width=50, rows=8, char="~")
  Add an argument for the swing size.
NEXT: learn next
lessons.code:
# Lesson 5: one function, three different waves.
import math
GOLD, RESET = "\033[38;2;201;168;76m", "\033[0m"

def wave(width, rows, char):
    for y in range(rows):
        x = int(width / 2 + (width / 2 - 1) * math.sin(y / 2))
        print(GOLD + " " * x + char + RESET)

wave(width=30, rows=10, char="*")
wave(width=60, rows=6, char="o")

lessons.title: 6. Randomness: a different result every time
lessons.text:
random.random() gives a number between 0 and 1. random.seed(7) makes it repeat the same way:
the seed is how a generative artist gets the SAME piece back.
TRY
  Run it three times: different each time. Then remove the # before random.seed(7): now it repeats.
NEXT: learn next
lessons.code:
# Lesson 6: a random walk, one step left or right per row.
import random
GOLD, RESET = "\033[38;2;201;168;76m", "\033[0m"
# random.seed(7)
x = 20
for y in range(25):
    x += random.choice([-2, -1, 0, 1, 2])
    x = max(0, min(40, x))
    print(GOLD + " " * x + "o" + RESET)

lessons.title: 7. Pictures: from text to pixels
lessons.text:
Pillow (PIL) draws real images. This saves a PNG to ~/Pictures/pieces.
SEE IT: on the iPad desktop, Home > Pictures > pieces, double-click the file.
TRY
  Change the colour (red, green, blue, each 0 to 255). Change width=4 to width=12.
NEXT: learn next
lessons.code:
# Lesson 7: draw a sine curve into a picture file.
import math, os
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
img = Image.new("RGB", (1200, 600), (14, 12, 8))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
pts = [(x, 300 + 200 * math.sin(x / 80)) for x in range(1200)]
d.line(pts, fill=(201, 168, 76), width=4)
out = os.path.expanduser("~/Pictures/pieces/lesson7.png")
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out), exist_ok=True)
img.save(out)
print("Saved", out)

lessons.title: 8. Parametric curves: two sines at once
lessons.text:
Feed one sine into x and another into y and you get loops (Lissajous curves).
The ratio of a to b decides the shape. This is the family your own curve work lives near.
TRY
  a, b = 3, 2  then 5, 4  then 7, 6. Then compare with the finished piece: piece lissajous 5 4
NEXT: learn next
lessons.code:
# Lesson 8: x and y each follow their own sine.
import math, os
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
a, b = 3, 2
S = 1000
img = Image.new("RGB", (S, S), (14, 12, 8))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
pts = []
for i in range(3001):
    t = i / 3000 * 2 * math.pi
    pts.append((S / 2 + math.sin(a * t) * 400, S / 2 + math.sin(b * t) * 400))
d.line(pts, fill=(201, 168, 76), width=3)
out = os.path.expanduser(f"~/Pictures/pieces/lesson8-{a}-{b}.png")
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out), exist_ok=True)
img.save(out)
print("Saved", out)

lessons.title: 9. Your own command (like the house's slash commands)
lessons.text:
A command is just a program in a folder the shell searches (~/bin) with permission to run.
DO, one line at a time:
  cp ~/learn/code/09_command.py ~/bin/curve
  chmod +x ~/bin/curve
  curve
The first line of the file (#!/usr/bin/env python3) tells Linux which language runs it.
You just made a command. Type curve from any folder, on the R1, the iPhone or the iPad.
NEXT: learn next
lessons.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Lesson 9: this file becomes your own command, `curve`.
import math, random
GOLD, RESET = "\033[38;2;201;168;76m", "\033[0m"
k = random.uniform(2, 5)
for y in range(18):
    x = int(20 + 18 * math.sin(y / k))
    print(GOLD + " " * x + "*" + RESET)

lessons.title: 10. Commands that take options
lessons.text:
sys.argv holds the words typed after the command: `curve 30 4` gives ["30", "4"].
DO
  cp ~/learn/code/10_arguments.py ~/bin/curve     (replaces your lesson 9 version)
  curve            curve 40         curve 40 6
TRY
  Add a third option for the character, so `curve 40 6 o` draws with o.
NEXT: learn next
lessons.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Lesson 10: curve [rows] [stretch]
import math, sys
GOLD, RESET = "\033[38;2;201;168;76m", "\033[0m"
rows = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 18
k = float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 3
for y in range(rows):
    x = int(20 + 18 * math.sin(y / k))
    print(GOLD + " " * x + "*" + RESET)

lessons.title: 11. Shortcuts: aliases in your shell
lessons.text:
An alias is a nickname for a longer command. They live in ~/.bashrc, read at every login.
DO
  nano ~/.bashrc     and add at the bottom:
      alias pics='ls -t ~/Pictures/pieces | head'
      alias again='piece flowfield'
  save, then:  source ~/.bashrc
  pics       again       pics
Small tools you make for yourself are how a terminal becomes yours.
NEXT: learn next

lessons.title: 12. Your first generative series
lessons.text:
A series: the same rules, many seeds, you keep the best. This makes 5 at once.
DO
  learn run         then look at them on the iPad (Home > Pictures > pieces)
  learn edit        and change the rules: the number of lines, the step size, the colours
Keep the seed of the one you like: the same seed always makes the same picture.
You are now writing generative art. Read the finished pieces next:  piece   then   piece flowfield -c
This is the last lesson. More come when you ask.
lessons.code:
# Lesson 12: five pieces from five seeds.
import math, os, random
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
os.makedirs(os.path.expanduser("~/Pictures/pieces"), exist_ok=True)
for seed in range(1, 6):
    random.seed(seed)
    W, H = 1000, 700
    img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), (14, 12, 8))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    f = random.uniform(0.003, 0.01)
    for _ in range(250):
        x, y = random.uniform(0, W), random.uniform(0, H)
        pts = [(x, y)]
        for _ in range(60):
            a = math.sin(x * f) * 3 + math.cos(y * f) * 3
            x, y = x + math.cos(a) * 5, y + math.sin(a) * 5
            pts.append((x, y))
        d.line(pts, fill=(201, 168, 76), width=1)
    out = os.path.expanduser(f"~/Pictures/pieces/series-{seed}.png")
    img.save(out)
    print("Saved", out)

lessons.title: Wave
lessons.text:
Three gold sine waves breathing across the terminal. Ctrl+C stops it.
Run it, then open its code and change one number.
lessons.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Three gold sine waves breathing across the terminal. Ctrl+C stops it.
import math, os, shutil, sys, time

GOLD = "\033[38;2;201;168;76m"   # the house gold, #c9a84c
DIM = "\033[38;2;110;92;42m"
RESET = "\033[0m"
frames = int(os.environ.get("FRAMES", "0"))   # 0 = forever (FRAMES=5 is how the setup tests it)

t, n = 0.0, 0
try:
    print("\033[?25l", end="")   # hide the cursor
    while True:
        w, h = shutil.get_terminal_size()
        h = max(6, h - 1)
        rows = [[" "] * w for _ in range(h)]
        for k, (amp, speed, char) in enumerate([(0.42, 1.0, "~"), (0.30, 1.6, "."), (0.18, 2.3, "o")]):
            for x in range(w):
                y = int(h / 2 + math.sin(x / 7 + t * speed + k) * h * amp)
                if 0 <= y < h:
                    rows[y][x] = char
        out = "\033[H" + "\n".join((GOLD if i % 2 else DIM) + "".join(r) for i, r in enumerate(rows)) + RESET
        sys.stdout.write(out); sys.stdout.flush()
        t += 0.12; n += 1
        if frames and n >= frames:
            break
        time.sleep(0.05)
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    pass
finally:
    print("\033[?25h" + RESET)

lessons.title: Spiral
lessons.text:
A golden-angle spiral of points, drawn once in the terminal.
Run it, then open its code and change one number.
lessons.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# A golden-angle spiral of points, drawn once in the terminal.
import math, shutil

GOLD, RESET = "\033[38;2;201;168;76m", "\033[0m"
w, h = shutil.get_terminal_size()
h = max(10, h - 2)
grid = [[" "] * w for _ in range(h)]
golden = math.pi * (3 - math.sqrt(5))          # about 137.5 degrees: how sunflower seeds pack
for i in range(1, 400):
    r = math.sqrt(i) / math.sqrt(400) * min(w / 2, h)   # terminal cells are twice as tall as wide
    a = i * golden
    x, y = int(w / 2 + r * math.cos(a)), int(h / 2 + r * math.sin(a) / 2)
    if 0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h:
        grid[y][x] = "*" if i % 13 == 0 else "."
print(GOLD + "\n".join("".join(r) for r in grid) + RESET)
print("Change 400 or the 13, run it again: piece spiral")

lessons.title: Lissajous
lessons.text:
A Lissajous curve saved as a picture. Try: piece lissajous 5 4
Run it, then open its code and change one number.
lessons.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# A Lissajous curve saved as a picture. Try: piece lissajous 5 4
import math, os, sys
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

a = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 3
b = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 2
size = 1200
img = Image.new("RGB", (size, size), (14, 12, 8))          # the house's dark ground
d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
pts = []
for i in range(4001):
    t = i / 4000 * 2 * math.pi
    pts.append((size / 2 + math.sin(a * t + math.pi / 2) * size * 0.42, size / 2 + math.sin(b * t) * size * 0.42))
d.line(pts, fill=(201, 168, 76), width=3)                  # the house gold
out = os.path.expanduser(f"~/Pictures/pieces/lissajous-{a}-{b}.png")
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out), exist_ok=True)
img.save(out)
print("Saved", out)
print("See it on the desktop: open Home > Pictures > pieces")

lessons.title: Flow field
lessons.text:
A flow field: 600 lines follow invisible currents. Different every run. Try: piece flowfield 7 (a seed)
Run it, then open its code and change one number.
lessons.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# A flow field: 600 lines follow invisible currents. Different every run. Try: piece flowfield 7 (a seed)
import math, os, random, sys, time
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

seed = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else int(time.time())
random.seed(seed)
W, H = 1600, 1100
img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), (14, 12, 8))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
f1, f2, f3 = random.uniform(0.002, 0.006), random.uniform(0.002, 0.006), random.uniform(0, 6.28)

def angle(x, y):
    return math.sin(x * f1 + f3) * 2.2 + math.cos(y * f2) * 2.2

for _ in range(600):
    x, y = random.uniform(0, W), random.uniform(0, H)
    pts = [(x, y)]
    for _ in range(80):
        a = angle(x, y)
        x, y = x + math.cos(a) * 4, y + math.sin(a) * 4
        if not (0 <= x < W and 0 <= y < H):
            break
        pts.append((x, y))
    g = random.randint(120, 201)
    if len(pts) > 2:
        d.line(pts, fill=(g, int(g * 0.84), int(g * 0.38)), width=1)
out = os.path.expanduser(f"~/Pictures/pieces/flowfield-{seed}.png")
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out), exist_ok=True)
img.save(out)
print("Saved", out, "(seed", str(seed) + ": the same seed makes the same picture)")

lessons.title: Harmonograph
lessons.text:
A harmonograph: two swinging pendulums with friction draw a fading spiral. Different every run.
Run it, then open its code and change one number.
lessons.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# A harmonograph: two swinging pendulums with friction draw a fading spiral. Different every run.
import math, os, random, time
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

seed = int(time.time()); random.seed(seed)
S = 1200
img = Image.new("RGB", (S, S), (14, 12, 8))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
f = [random.choice([2, 3, 4]) + random.uniform(-0.02, 0.02) for _ in range(4)]   # near-whole ratios make the loops
p = [random.uniform(0, math.pi) for _ in range(4)]
damp = 0.0025
pts = []
for i in range(30000):
    t = i * 0.02
    e = math.exp(-damp * t)
    x = math.sin(f[0] * t + p[0]) * e + math.sin(f[1] * t + p[1]) * e
    y = math.sin(f[2] * t + p[2]) * e + math.sin(f[3] * t + p[3]) * e
    pts.append((S / 2 + x * S * 0.22, S / 2 + y * S * 0.22))
for i in range(0, len(pts) - 1, 50):                      # fade from gold to dark as the swing dies
    k = 1 - i / len(pts)
    d.line(pts[i:i + 51], fill=(int(40 + 161 * k), int(34 + 134 * k), int(16 + 60 * k)), width=2)
out = os.path.expanduser(f"~/Pictures/pieces/harmonograph-{seed}.png")
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out), exist_ok=True)
img.save(out)
print("Saved", out)
